title: I made 84 monster animations, then wrote a checker that found 44 problems I couldn't see by eye
author: Big-Communication950
selftext:
Last week I made a pack of 12 low poly enemies (skeletons, orc, goblin, slime, spider, mimic chest and more), each with 7 clips: idle, walk, run, attack, hit, death and taunt. 84 clips in total.



Every clip looked fine in my preview renders. Then I wrote a small script that plays every clip in Blender, frame by frame, and measures the actual mesh:



\- the lowest point of the body on every frame (does anything sink through the floor?)

\- the first and last frame of each loop (does the loop close cleanly?)

\- whether attack, hit and taunt end exactly where idle starts (no pop when you switch clips)

\- the biggest jump between two frames (catches broken keys)



First run: 44 problems. Nearly all were bodies sinking into the floor: death clips ended 30 to 50 cm under the ground, a golem's feet sat 6 cm deep, a spider's legs dipped through when it reared up, and a bat's attack ended on a different wing beat than its idle, so it popped.



The fix that helped most was a small "floor solver": after each clip is made, it measures the lowest point on every frame and lifts the root by a smoothed amount, but never touches the first and last frame, so the clip still blends into idle. A few attacks needed real pose changes instead.



Second run: 2 problems (a crouch pushing the feet down). Third run: 0.



Lesson for me: preview renders show you a few frames, but a checker sees all of them. Happy to share more about the checks if anyone's doing animation work.



(The assets are AI-assisted and that's disclosed on the store page.)

comments.body: Free sampler with the skeleton and slime (GLB + FBX, Godot / Unity): [https://soresa-assets.itch.io/free-stylized-animated](https://soresa-assets.itch.io/free-stylized-animated)

comments.author: Redditry199
comments.body:
the axe is flipped, the skeletons dont actually fall but duck, the goblin/orc has stiff hands and legs on death animation, the tongue on the mimic is glitching.

If this is the 0 problem you gotta reconsider what your flow.

replies.author: Big-Communication950
replies.body: Thanks, this is really useful feedback. You're right: my checker only measured technical things (floor sinking, loop seams, popping between clips), not whether a motion actually looks right. It even caused one of these: the floor fix lifted the skeletons' collapse into a crouch. I'm fixing the skeleton deaths, the goblin/orc death poses, the mimic tongue and the axe orientation, and I'll post an update. Appreciate you taking the time to look closely.

replies.author: Big-Communication950
replies.body: Update: version 1.1 is out with all four fixes. The skeletons now buckle to their knees and fall onto their side, the goblin/orc/zombie/golem deaths have bent knees and elbows and loose hands, the mimic's tongue stays inside whenever the lid isn't wide open, and the orc's axe edge faces the right way with a slower 9-frame chop. I also changed my process: I now check every clip with frame-by-frame strips, not just the automatic checker. Thanks again, this made the pack better.

replies.author: Itchy-Individual3536
replies.body: it's funny, when I made my AI generate meshes for monsters with axes, they came also out as flipped initially :D

replies.author: Big-Communication950
replies.body: Ha, glad it's not just me! Fixed in 1.1 now.

comments.author: Twisted-Fingers
comments.body: Honestly, the movements doesnt looks like animations

replies.author: Big-Communication950
replies.body: Fair point. They're simple keyframed animations, so they're stiffer than hand-made work. What feels most off to you: the timing, the lack of weight and follow-through, or the way the joints bend? I'd like to improve them.

replies.author: Big-Communication950
replies.body: That's a really good point, thanks. I'll make a non-humanoid creature pack: the bat, mimic, slime and spider plus new creatures in the same style. I'll post here when it's ready.
